A join of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory under PadicFamilies, an id already carried by PAPER-PILLONI-20, which proposed it, and by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21 and -25; the title reproduces the parent's atlas title exactly and `padic` is a galaxy id. The 247 items are the paper itself — ordinary cohomology with partial support for dynamic correspondences in the abstract, the Iwahori-level integral models and the Cousin spectral sequence, the higher Hida complexes $M^•_w$ over $\Lambda$ with their duality, and the comparison with higher Coleman theory. None of it is owned upstream, where PadicFamilies plans ordinary projectors and eigenvarieties in degree 0. Large but coherent, and it is the natural continuation of the roadmap this paper's predecessor proposed.

Accept. A join of IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes under AutomorphicBundles, proposed by PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 and carried by four other extractions. The 20 items are the parts of §§2 and 4.3 that are general theory of coherent cohomological correspondences rather than steps of the Hida argument — solid correspondences with their restriction and trace maps, the transpose and the duality of Theorem 2.7.4, the normalised operators on automorphic bundles — and they sit above what B3–B5 own.

Accept. A join of ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII under ShimuraVarieties, an id carried by nine other extractions and proposed by PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22. Four items only, and they are exactly the integral-model inputs of §§3.4.19–3.4.22 and 4.1.1: de Jong's stacks $\mathcal A_{g,d}$ with $p\mid d$ allowed, their polarization-type loci, normalisation as a definition of integral models, and the self-dual chain of isogenies at Iwahori level. E63, confirmed, is about the definition of those type loci and does not affect the routing.

Accept. A join of ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary under ShimuraCompactifications, proposed by PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 and carried by two others. Two items, the partial toroidal compactification of the ordinary Igusa tower and the extension of the group schemes $\mathrm{Gr}_i$ over the boundary, which the parent's C5 does not reach; E67, confirmed, is precisely about the second of these, which supports the routing rather than undermining it.

Accept, and this is the paper's own proposal rather than a join: no other extraction carries IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentrationPartIISiegelOrdinary. notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-7b31c4, issue #1200, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by Claude Code, session cc-72825f (issue #1199, PR #2307). Source read: the authors' version on V. Pilloni's homepage, higherhidaSiegel.pdf, 65 pages, built 5 November 2025, whose recorded sha256 af70d084612b1b75761694923ef2395752d23b41e0b8b458910d096df4c8c3c6 reproduces byte for byte. The published Inventiones text is paywalled and was not compared, as the extraction states; every locator is a page of this version, printed page equal to PDF page, and that boundary is right.

Findings. All 133 sourceIssues now carry verdicts and all 133 are confirmed: 14 errors, 28 gaps, 91 misprints. Nothing was rejected, nothing deleted, and I add no finding of my own. For each I located the quoted text on the page its locator names and checked the correction against the paper's own conventions; where the correction is a computation or a combinatorial claim I redid it.

A striking number are settled by the paper contradicting itself, which is the strongest evidence available when only one version is in hand, and I checked each of those pairs directly: C(kappa) is defined with dominance in X*(T) on p. 3 and in X*(T)_Q on p. 48 (E3); the higher Hida complexes are defined with an ordinary tensor product on p. 5 and a completed one on p. 56 (E9); kappa is defined from nu on p. 5 and from nu_alg on p. 56 (E10); Proposition 4.1.13(3) gives D_{g-k} where its own proof gives D_{g-k-1} (E69); Z_i is defined with clashing indices on p. 42 and correctly on p. 45 (E71); Lemma 4.3.6 removes a sum to g in its statement and to an undefined d five times around it (E85); Proposition 6.2.13 states A/p^n and proves A/p^r (E130); Proposition 2.3.5 states H^i(X, j_!F) and proves H^i(X-bar, j_!F) (E24).

The substantive findings I checked in more detail. E45 is a genuine error: Lemma 2.10.1(4) claims finite cohomology for RGamma_Z(Y,F) with no boundedness on F, and i^! of an unbounded complex over k[x]/(x^2) breaks it. E122 is another: the second halves of Proposition 6.2.3(2)-(3) are false as inequalities of divisors, because part (1) of the same proposition orders D_{+,eps} and D_{+,eps'} the other way; what holds is the inclusion of supports. E63 is a third: the polarization-type substacks A_{g,delta} are defined by an etale-local condition that mu_{delta_i} cannot satisfy when p divides delta_i, which is exactly the case section 4.1.1 needs. The gaps that matter most are E25 (Corollary 2.3.14 needs the two maps of line bundles to lie over the structure maps, or the limit and colimit do not exist), E28 (the ordinary-part construction is not available in a triangulated category, as the paper's own footnote 2 concedes), E42 (Proposition 2.9.9 needs p_1 proper for its trace), E100 (Theorem 4.5.2 restricts the Cousin sum to C(kappa) without saying why the other summands have no ordinary part) and E126 (T^{++} generating T(Q_p) as a group does not propagate a lower bound on slopes; a cone argument does).

Limits of my check. This PDF's text layer drops all citation brackets and all author names in the bibliography, so I could not verify any citation key from the source. For the two findings about the numbering inside [BP21] (E114, E129) I therefore rely on the extraction's reading of arXiv:2110.10251; E114 is a defect either way, since the references within one section cannot all belong to one version of that paper. The text layer also does not separate subscripts from superscripts, so for E34-style glyph positions - here E47 (interior marks and the sign on D) and E98 (K_p for K^p) - I rely on the extraction's renders and say so in those verdicts. In every such case the surrounding definitions settle the substance independently.

Two printed slips are recorded by no finding: 'the the closure' in the proof of Proposition 4.4.4 (p. 51), and, in the same vicinity, nothing else. I leave it for a later pass rather than manufacture a finding.

Structure, verified in full. 417 items (372 missing, 37 planned, 8 library) and 22 routes: 17 source, 5 Part II. Every missing item is routed exactly once. All source stage ids resolve, including AnalyticStacks:AS.0/AS.2/AS.3 and SolidAnalyticRings:SA.3, which are absent from data/atlas.json but present in research/blueprint/roadmaps/, where stages are keyed by 'key' rather than 'id' - a checker reading only 'id' reports them missing, and four other extractions route to AnalyticStacks the same way. All 72 planned references of Stage:Layer form resolve in data/atlas.json; the other 8 use the corpus-wide tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/...#layer-... form whose targets live in the Tau Ceti repository. All five Part II titles reproduce their parents' atlas titles exactly and all five areas are galaxy ids. Four of the five Part II routes join proposals that the corpus already contains - HigherHidaAndColemanTheory from PAPER-PILLONI-20, IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes from PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18, ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII from PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 and ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary from PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 - and the fifth, IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentrationPartIISiegelOrdinary, is this paper's own, carried by no other extraction, with its parent present in the atlas.

One correction made in place: the extraction recorded no libraryPins; I added them, Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 and Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. All 60 cited declarations resolve at those pins.

Correction to this review (23 September 2026, cc-7b31c4). The first version of this review reported that mathlib:CommRing.orzechProperty, cited on the item ext-nakayama-lemma, does not exist at the pin, and removed the citation. That was wrong and the citation has been restored: the declaration is `instance (priority := 100) CommRing.orzechProperty (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : OrzechProperty R` at Mathlib/RingTheory/FiniteType.lean:625, and it is what supplies the OrzechProperty hypothesis of OrzechProperty.bijective_of_surjective_of_finrank_le over a commutative ring. The false negative came from the shared declaration index, which carries no declaration written as `instance (priority := ...) Name`; Mathlib has 1033 of them at this pin. A citation must not be deleted on the index alone; the pinned source settles it.

What this review did not do. I did not read all 65 pages line by line; I read the pages every finding names, the statements the routes cite, and the surrounding material needed to judge them. I did not compare the published Inventiones text, so no finding here has been checked against the version of record. scripts/check_paper.py and research/blueprint/intake.py check-files both pass.
